- Ben to draft SCC variant + a 1-paragraph fallback we can insert into the Order Form (see proposed-sccs-text.txt attached).

Olga / Laura / Kevin — thanks. I took a pass and pushed a short compromise that should be acceptable for procurement while protecting our Serving/DR routing. High-level summary below and attached redline PDF (Attachment: hosting-variance-ticket-#7421.pdf).

My recommendations (contract language bullets you can paste):
- Pilot hosting carveout: Redwood will restrict processing to US-based regions for the "Pilot Environment" as defined in the Order Form for an initial period of 90 days from go-live. Any extension beyond 90 days requires mutual written consent and a technical runbook documenting the changes and fallback routing.
- SCC variant: use the standard SCC text with an explicit Annex reference: "See Annex X (Hosting Variance — Pilot)". Annex X will restate the limited US-only commitment and the 90-day maximum; Annex X is time-boxed and cannot be used to amend underlying SCC obligations.
- Roles: propose we accept a committed "subprocessor registry" clause: we will provide a fielded registry during onboarding and notify customers 30 days before adding any subprocessor. For Luma's auditors who need field-level mapping, offer a scoped evidence package (field mappings + SOC2 scope note) under a mutual NDA/limited disclosure exhibit.

SLA / Exec clearance ask: Because the pilot requires region-bound routing, our infra team requests a small SLO carveout for failover that allows cross-region fallback for up to 60 seconds in the event of pod-level outage. This is operationally necessary; it is not bulk export. If Luma needs an explicit export prohibition, we should require a temporary exception dataset and compensating controls. Given this is higher risk than standard, I recommend we offer a one-time credit (2% of monthly committed fee) if we invoke fallback cross-region routing during the pilot. Please confirm if, from procurement/legal POV, Luma would accept the credit + fallback wording instead of an outright no-fallback promise.

If Luma agrees in principle I can prepare: (a) the Annex X text; (b) Order Form snippet; (c) one-paragraph DocuSign cover for their procurement team.
